page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-96-lssd is a server instance from the c4d family, built on the x86_64 CPU architecture. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs and 372.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory allocation of approximately 3.88 GB per core. The instance does not include any GPU accelerators.

A defining characteristic of this configuration is its integrated local storage subsystem. It comes bundled with 3221 GB of local NVMe SSD storage distributed across 8 local SSDs. This high-speed local storage is directly attached to the instance, providing low-latency data access. The instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a resource density perspective, the c4d-standard-96-lssd offers a balanced ratio of compute to memory alongside a substantial local storage footprint. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high-capacity, low-latency scratch space or local caching without the overhead of network-attached storage. Appropriate workloads include large-scale databases, data warehousing, high-performance web serving, and intensive data processing tasks that benefit from dedicated CPU cores and high-speed local NVMe drives.
